sections.h2: Who values property in Abilene, and who sets the tax?
sections.html:
Taylor Central Appraisal District values every parcel in the county, while the city, county, school district and other units each set their own rate. The district's FAQ says plainly that it controls market value and has no say over rates or the final bill.

Its office is at 1534 S Treadaway Blvd, Abilene, staffed on weekdays during business hours, with a mailing box at P.O. Box 1800 and a phone line at (325) 676-9381. A drop box sits in front of the building for forms. Exemption forms can also go by email to exemptions@cadtx.org, and protest forms to arbprotest@cadtx.org.

After a sale, the district receives the deed once it is filed with the county clerk. Handing over the recorded document number, or emailing a scan to customerservice@cadtx.org, speeds up the ownership change.

sections.h2: What property tax rate did Abilene's council set for fiscal 2027?
sections.html:
Council set 74.95 cents per $100 of taxable value, a hair under the prior 75.06 cents, when it adopted the $414.6 million operating budget on Sept. 10, 2026. The fiscal year starts Oct. 1.

A lower rate did not mean smaller bills for everyone. The city's own budget summary estimates an average 4.2 percent tax increase on existing property because values rose, and says new construction accounts for $16.8 million of the $18.3 million increase in total property tax revenue. The city's home page also notes that the adopted rate raises more maintenance and operations revenue than the year before.

sections.h2: What does the city plan to spend the money on?
sections.html:
The budget release lists street work, drainage and public safety near the top. Street projects named include Barrow Street Phase I, Griffith Road Phase II, Maple Street North Phase II and two work zones in Richland Acres, plus $430,000 to assess pavement conditions citywide.

  • Drainage: the first stormwater project targets recurring flooding near the downtown railroad underpasses.
  • Water: money continues for the Northeast Water Treatment Plant, and planning covers the proposed Cedar Ridge Reservoir.
  • Housing: $1.5 million goes to Rebuild ABI for renovated or new affordable homes.
  • Public safety: three added officers and 21 patrol vehicles.
  • Recreation: longer evening and weekend hours at the Sears and G.V. Daniels centers.

Other lines show where growth shows up: the airport gets $148,000 for maintenance staffing as commercial service expands to Denver, Houston and Phoenix, the Convention Center gets $450,000 for kitchen equipment, and the zoo begins adding staff ahead of new exhibits and a cafe expected in summer 2027. Council also approved a one-time $13.5 million contribution to the Abilene Firemen's Relief and Retirement Fund, paid from the same data center sales tax revenue, which lifts that fund's projected funded ratio from about 45 percent to 52 percent.

The city also expects a one-time $19.3 million sales tax surplus tied to data center construction and says it is spending that on projects, vehicles and equipment rather than building it into ongoing costs. Sellers near those corridors may see construction while a home is listed.

sections.h2: When is an Abilene bill due and what does lateness cost?
sections.html:
Bills go out in October and are payable on receipt, but most owners can wait until Jan. 31 without penalty. Anything unpaid on Feb. 1 is delinquent and picks up a six percent penalty and one percent interest the same day.

The penalty then grows a point each month until July 1, when it reaches 12 percent, while interest keeps running at a point a month. A unit with a collection attorney can add up to 20 percent more. Seniors and disabled homeowners can split a homestead bill into four payments, and some collectors offer plans stretching to 36 months on a delinquent residence homestead.

sections.h2: Which exemptions does Taylor CAD apply to an Abilene home?
sections.html:
A home you own and live in on Jan. 1 qualifies for the general homestead exemption, and filing costs nothing. Nobody has to be hired to file it, and you do not reapply each year unless it asks in writing or you move.

  • Turning 65: the extra exemption is added on its own when the district already has your birth date, and applying at any point in that year earns the full year.
  • Mobile home on land you do not own: include the title or a verified purchase contract.
  • Home with a business inside: a homestead apportionment may be available.
  • Nonprofits: no automatic exemption from a federal tax-exempt status, and applications are due by April 30.

Texas law has school districts take $140,000 off a homestead, with a further $60,000 for older or disabled owners. Disabled veterans use a separate sliding scale, with a total exemption at a 100 percent rating.

sections.h2: How does a protest work at the Abilene appraisal district?
sections.html:
You protest market value only. Taylor CAD explains that assessed value is a formula and cannot be protested, and that a high bill from a high rate is not a protest ground. Notices of appraised value go out by April 1 or soon after, and the deadline is normally May 31, or a month after the notice arrives if that is later, and each notice prints its own cutoff.

File by mail, email, the drop box or the online portal. You may be offered an informal meeting with an appraiser first, which ends the case if you agree. Otherwise the formal hearing is at the district's Treadaway Boulevard office, and a notice arrives at least 15 days ahead.

  • Bring paper copies of comparable sales, a recent purchase price and photos of defects.
  • Expect three to five minutes per side and about 15 minutes in the room.
  • One postponement is allowed if no agent represents you.
  • Skipping the hearing gets the protest dismissed, and you have four days to ask for a reopening.

Landlords and small business owners in Abilene also deal with the district's business personal property side. Renditions listing furniture, equipment and inventory are due by April 15, an extension to May 15 requires a written request by April 15, and skipping the filing brings a 10 percent penalty on the taxes ultimately imposed. Rendition forms live on the district's Forms page.

Further appeals go to district court, binding arbitration or, for values above $1 million, the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

sections.h2: What should an Abilene seller know about unpaid taxes?
sections.html:
The county's lien for the year attaches on January 1, so a sale later in the year still carries that year's bill, and the title company normally pays it out of proceeds. Buyers should confirm which exemptions are on the account before closing.

New owners can claim their own homestead for the remainder of the tax year if the previous owner did not. The 10 percent yearly limit on assessed value begins the year after an exemption is first granted, so a new owner's clock starts fresh.

faqs.q: Who sets the Abilene property tax rate?
faqs.a: Each taxing unit does. Abilene's council set the city rate of 74.95 cents per $100 for fiscal 2027, and the county, school district and other units set theirs. Taylor CAD only values property.

faqs.q: Can I protest my Abilene tax bill?
faqs.a: Not the bill itself. You can protest market value with Taylor CAD, normally by May 31 or a month after your notice. The rate is outside its control.

faqs.q: Where is the Taylor Central Appraisal District?
faqs.a: 1534 S Treadaway Blvd, Abilene, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 1800, Abilene, TX 79604-1800. Phone (325) 676-9381, weekdays 8 am to 5 pm.

faqs.q: Do I need to reapply for my Abilene homestead exemption each year?
faqs.a: No. It continues unless the chief appraiser asks for a new application in writing or you move.

faqs.q: When do Abilene taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On Feb. 1, so pay by Jan. 31. Six percent penalty and one percent interest start then.
